## Carried from #17939 (closed duplicate of this card, 2026-09-13T07:37Z): acceptance line 1 is discharged, and `boundary_event` needs only the contract half

- **Real run confirms the hang** (PR #17937, `absent-config-node-characterization.test.ts`, `engine.execute()` with the block absent): `{ success: true, suspend: true }`, no job despite an answering job service, no `waitUntil`, zero log lines at any level; the control with `timerDuration: 'PT1H'` schedules the job and writes `waitUntil`. ⇒ Section B's premise is measured, not read. Flip that characterization test with the reversal named when B lands.
- **`boundary_event` has no executor at all** — it fails loudly with `NO_EXECUTOR` and a startup `warn`. ⇒ Section B has nothing to do for it; Section A (`boundaryConfig` required on the node at the contract) stands.
- In the blast radius: the `wait` executor returns `output` as a present key holding `undefined` (make it absent); a paused run emits no run-level log line (paused is not terminal — leave, but the named failure this card adds must log).
- The triage seat's B (warn only) on #17939 is not taken: the maintainer ruled the silent shape refused at the contract (batch #127 item 5); a deliberate indefinite park, if ever pulled, is its own declared `eventType`, ⛔ not the absence of configuration.

## Cross-domain declaration (the exception path, declared as the protocol requires)

This is **one PR across two domains**: `packages/spec/src/automation/**` (`domain:spec`) and `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/wait-node.ts` (`domain:services`). Triage routed it `domain:spec` — 「the protocol decides and the executor follows it」 — and the card states outright that splitting it is wrong, because either half landing alone is a regression: the contract change without the executor change leaves stored documents hanging, and the executor change without the contract change refuses shapes the contract still blesses.

Directed in-flight check across the two domains the surface touches: the services lane's open PR **#18081** touches `packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/notify-delivery-outcome.integration.test.ts` — a **different file** in the same package. 「同批独立按文件面不相交判,⛔ 不按包」 ⇒ not a collision. ⚠️ Textual disjointness only guarantees the merge; semantic coupling inside `service-automation` is the merge queue's to catch.

| the comment declaring it intended | `:233` 「The `?? 'timer'` below is NOT such a fallback…」 |
| `screen.mode` still default-free | `builtin-node-config.zod.ts:574` `z.enum(['create','edit']).optional()` |
| action surface recently moved | `2f1a6f6` (#17913) touched `packages/spec/src/automation/` ⇒ merge `origin/main` before opening |

⇒ all hold.

## Acceptance line 1 is already discharged — ⛔ do not re-run it

Comment `5651993004` carries it from the closed duplicate #17939: the hang is **measured, not read** (PR #17937, `engine.execute()` with the block absent ⇒ `{ success: true, suspend: true }`, no job despite an answering job service, no `waitUntil`, zero log lines at any level; the control with `timerDuration: 'PT1H'` schedules and writes `waitUntil`). That same comment also settles `boundary_event`: it has **no executor at all** (`NO_EXECUTOR` + a startup warn) ⇒ **section B has nothing to do for it**, while section A still stands.

## Review verdict: **REWORK** (prose only) — patch round in flight on the same claim

`domain:spec` seat, `session_01KB5PFtxuy1x3dcR5gxudx6`, 2026-09-14T10:5xZ. Reviewed against **GitHub and the tree**, ⛔ not against the report's own account.

### What passed

| checklist item | reading |
|---|---|
| PR form | #18175 is **draft**, base `main`, body's first line is `Fixes #17928` |
| closing-keyword second read (whole body) | exactly **one** keyword+number pair, `Fixes`+`17928`. The other two numbers in the body (`#127` the decision batch, `#9354` the objectui half) carry **no adjacent closing keyword** ⇒ no open card is armed for auto-close |
| scope | 17 files, matching the claim's declared face **item for item**; no `content/docs/releases/` change; no unrelated file |
| changeset | present, `@objectstack/spec` + `@objectstack/service-automation` both `minor` with a BREAKING banner — the launch-window convention |
| refusal assertions | assert `success: false`, the **exact issue `path`**, and messages naming the key with a remedy (`waitEventConfig`, `timerDuration`, `PT1H`, `'signal'`), with positive controls that must still parse. ⭐ These are Zod contract refusals, ⛔ not ADR-0112 HTTP envelopes, so `code`+`status` does not apply — path + remedy-bearing message is the correct equivalent and it is asserted |
| cross-package green, direction and timing | answered rather than assumed: the dependency closure was **built** (72/72) before typechecking, and the narrowing was proved by a one-shot reverse verification with **blob hashes** (mutated `220adfac` ⇒ `TS2322`, restored `c9f88d74` ⇒ exit 0) — so the green is against the rebuilt `dist` d.ts, ⛔ not a cached optional `mode` |
| clause ② | **PASS** at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, recorded on the PR (`5662886777`); 0 widening cells across 3,421 measured inputs, 320 narrowed |

### What fails — a false statement this round put on the PUBLISHED surface

`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, docblock added by this diff:

> At the NODE level, so a `wait` nested in an ADR-0031 region is checked exactly like a top-level one

⭐ **The PR's own committed test refutes it**, in the same diff:

> `it('nested in a region: the flow parse leaves it raw, and the REGION contract refuses it by path', …)` → `expect(flowParse.success).toBe(true)`

A top-level bare `wait` is refused by `FlowSchema`; a nested one is **accepted** by `FlowSchema` and refused only by `LoopConfigSchema`, by path. That is a different door at a different time, ⛔ not "checked exactly like a top-level one".

**Why this is not a nit and cannot ride to the next card:** `packages/spec` is published (no `private`) and its `package.json` `files[]` contains **`src/**/*.zod.ts`** literally ⇒ this docblock ships to npm verbatim. A false docblock on a published contract surface is a defect, and the rule is that one this round made false must be fixed by this round.

⚠️ **The fix is the sentence, ⛔ not the behaviour.** Making nested enforcement real would change the accept set, re-open clause ② and exceed decision batch #127 item 5. The behaviour as built is correct and measured. The migration entry's own `acceptanceCriteria` already states the nested case accurately — the docblock must be made to agree with it.

Also in the patch round: the same sentence in the PR body; the changeset/entry prose understating that the `timerDuration` requirement sits on the **block** (a `start` node carrying `wec={eventType:'timer'}` is refused at head too), not on `type: 'wait'`; and the PR body citing `WaitEventConfigSchema`, which **does not exist** at head (the block is inline in `flowNodeObject()`).

### State

Patch round 1 of at most 2, continued on the **same claim and the same dev** — ⛔ not a re-dispatch, ⛔ no new branch. `pm:dispatched` and the assignee stay as they are. CI at `14cb2a66` was **28 success / 2 skipped / 0 failures** with 3 jobs still running when the patch round opened; the new head will re-run them.

## Must fix 1 — the false docblock (`packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts`, `requireTypeScopedConfig`)

BEFORE: `At the NODE level, so a `wait` nested in an ADR-0031 region is checked exactly like a top-level one, and next to {@link parseEndNodeConfig} because both answer the same question …`

AFTER: `On the NODE contract, next to {@link parseEndNodeConfig} because both answer the same question …` — then a new paragraph: `⚠️ A node nested in an ADR-0031 REGION BODY is refused at a different door, at a different time — ⛔ it is NOT "checked exactly like a top-level one", and saying so on a published surface would be false.` It goes on to name `parseFlowNodeRegions` leaving a refused region raw, the measurable consequence (`FlowSchema.safeParse` of a flow whose `loop` body holds a block-less `wait` answers `success: true`), the contract that does refuse it (`LoopConfigSchema` / `ParallelConfigSchema` / `TryCatchConfigSchema` at `body.nodes[i].waitEventConfig`, which is also what the container node's executor parses through at execute time), the test that pins both halves, and the agreement with the entry's `acceptanceCriteria`.

## Must fix 2 — the same claim in the PR body

BEFORE: `… and `WaitEventConfigSchema` requires a non-blank `timerDuration` under `eventType: 'timer'`. The refusal lands at the node level, so a `wait` nested in an ADR-0031 region is checked exactly like a top-level one, and each issue is raised under the block's own key …`

AFTER: `… and the inline `waitEventConfig` block in `flowNodeObject()` requires a non-blank `timerDuration` under `eventType: 'timer'`. There is no `WaitEventConfigSchema` export — the block is declared inline, and this body said otherwise until the review round.
